# Interior lighting and mirror color changes

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Pull wiring harness, remove cover, swap original LED for white 1206 SMD with gray overlay, and reinstall mirror. [t758]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Pull the wiring harness from the back of the mirror by pressing one tap while pulling.
2. Remove the plastic cover at the base where the mirror attaches to the windshield.
3. Loosen the mount screw with a T15 Torx screwdriver without fully removing it.
4. Lay a towel on a surface and place the mirror face down on top of it.
5. [Partial] Pry up an edge near the top using a plastic trim tool in a spot not visible when installed.
6. Continue prying around the perimeter until the entire cover comes off.
7. Pull the circuit board out from inside the housing.
8. Disconnect the harness connector from the back of the board.
9. Locate the existing LED on the board facing inward within its slot.
10. Note the polarity direction of the current LED before removing it.
11. [Partial] Heat up one end of the original LED where it attaches to the board with a soldering iron.
12. Slide the heated LED off the board and set it aside.
13. Lay the new white 1206 SMD LED into the same slot on the board.
14. [Partial] Heat up the connectors of the new LED until they attach securely to the board.
15. [Partial] Place a gray adhesive overlay over the top of the new LED where it faces outward.
16. Use a razor blade to cut underneath the dark blue display overlay on the map and temperature light.
17. Cut the new blue adhesive film into the same shape as the removed piece.
18. Apply two strips of the blue adhesive followed by a single gray strip over the display area.
19. Lay the circuit board back inside the mirror housing.
20. Reattach the small harness connector to the board.
21. Line up all components and press the trim section back onto the housing.
22. [Partial] Take the reassembled mirror back to the truck and reinstall it on the windshield.

_Procedure reported by [t758]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-change-gentex-mirror-color-to-blue.8971/>_

## Tools

- T15 Torx screwdriver [t758]
- Plastic trim removal tool [t758]

## Parts

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a towel under the mirror to prevent scratches during disassembly. [t758]
- [Partial] Pry at an inconspicuous spot like the top edge of the housing first. [t758]
